name: Abner
description: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy

points: When Saul saw David go forth against the Philistine, he asked Abner, the captain of the host, Whose son is this youth? And Abner could not tell; in the shock of it they forgot whose son the young man was.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: And as David returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, Abner took him, and brought him before Saul with the head of the Philistine in his hand. Imagine, he has got this big Philistine's head in his hand. He shows up like, hey, what is going on, king?

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: As David returned from the slaughter of the Philistine with the head of the Philistine in his hand, Abner brought him before Saul, and David answered, I am the son of thy servant Jesse the Bethlehemite.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

points: David beheld the place where Saul lay, with Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his host; Saul lay in the trench with his spear stuck in the ground at his bolster, and the people pitched round about him as protection to the king.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: This is when Saul was hunting David to kill him, because Saul was dealing with bitterness, envy, and hatred. David and Abishai came down to the camp by night, and Saul lay sleeping in the trench, with Abner, the top warrior in Israel at that time, and the people round about him.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: David went over to the other side, stood on the top of an hill afar off, and cried to Abner: Art not thou a valiant man? and who is like to thee in Israel? wherefore then hast thou not kept thy lord the king? for there came one of the people in to destroy the king thy lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

points: Abner and the servants of Ishbosheth met Joab and the servants of David at the pool of Gibeon, sitting on opposite sides. Abner said, Let the young men arise and play, meaning let them compete and battle one another; the Lord is a man of war, and such contests were done in that day.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: When Asahel refused to turn aside, Abner smote him with the hinder end of the spear under the fifth rib, and he died there. A strong thrust is needed to drive a spear through a man, and Abner was strong. Those who came to the place stood still; the lesson is to take heed to the warning and not keep testing a man.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Joab and Abishai pursued Abner until sundown, and the children of Benjamin gathered to Abner in one troop and stood on the top of a hill. Abner had rounded up his men and stood ready.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Abner called to Joab, asking whether the sword should devour forever, and warned that it would be bitterness in the latter end; he asked how long before Joab bade the people return from following their brethren. Joab answered that unless Abner had spoken, the people would have gone up in the morning, and he blew the trumpet and the people stood still and fought no more.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Abner and his men walked all that night and came to Mahanaim. Of David's servants nineteen men and Asahel were missing, but they had smitten of Abner's men three hundred and threescore. They buried Asahel at Bethlehem, and Joab and his men came to Hebron at break of day.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Abner made himself strong for the house of Saul. When Ishbosheth charged him over Rizpah, Saul's concubine, Abner was very wroth, saying he had shown kindness to the house of Saul and not delivered them to David, and now was charged with a fault concerning this woman.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: Michal was taken from her husband Phaltiel, who went weeping behind her until Abner told him to return. David was taking back what was his as the king before the Lord.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: Abner spoke with the elders of Israel and with Benjamin, reminding them they had sought David in times past, and that the Lord had said by the hand of David He would save Israel out of the hand of the Philistines and all their enemies. Abner came to David at Hebron with twenty men, David made them a feast, and Abner went in peace to gather all Israel to David.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: Joab returned from pursuing a troop and heard that Abner had come and been sent away in peace. Joab came to the king and said Abner had come to deceive him and to know his going out and coming in; he did not trust Abner, and there was already blood between them, for Abner had killed Asahel his brother.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: Joab, without David's knowledge, sent messengers after Abner and brought him back to Hebron, took him aside in the gate to speak quietly, and smote him there under the fifth rib, that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.
It was payback; Joab's blood was burning for revenge. Abner was unwise to return to that place, knowing what Joab would do, but it was of the Lord.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: When David heard it, he declared himself and his kingdom guiltless before the Lord forever from the blood of Abner, and laid it on the head of Joab and all his father's house. He commanded Joab and all the people to rend their clothes and gird with sackcloth and mourn before Abner, and the king himself followed the coffin.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: When Saul's son Ishbosheth heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands were feeble and all the Israelites were troubled.

note.label: 2 Samuel 4: The Slaying of Ishbosheth

points: David commanded his young men, and they slew Rechab and Baanah, cut off their hands and feet, and hanged them up over the pool in Hebron, but took the head of Ishbosheth and buried it in the sepulchre of Abner. The Most High has His own way of doing things; His people are not to put the cart before the horse.

note.label: 2 Samuel 4: The Slaying of Ishbosheth

points: Joab, who had turned after Adonijah, flees to the tabernacle of the Lord and catches hold of the horns of the altar, but Solomon sends Benaiah to fall upon him. Joab dies for the innocent blood he shed when he slew Abner and Amasa, two men more righteous and better than he, without David's knowledge.

note.label: 1 Kings 2: The Charge to Solomon and the Kingdom Established
